etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Inherited from Middle English prudent, from Old French prudent, from Latin prūdēns, contracted from prōvidēns (“foresight”) (English providence), the present participle of prōvideō (“to forsee; to provide for”). Unrelated to prude. Doublet of provident. Displaced native Old English glēaw.
senses: Sagacious in adapting means to ends; circumspect in action, or in determining any line of conduct.
